title: Canonized, Sainted: Participle Titles for Legacy

sections.content: István's greatest posthumous title uses this same pattern: *szentté avatott* ("canonized", literally "made into a saint"). The verb *szentté avat* is a compound built from *szent* ("saint, holy") plus the translative ending *-vá/-vé* ("into"), which you know from A2 Unit 35. The fixed expression *szentté avat* then gives the participle *szentté avatott*.

items.spanish: A szentté avatott király ma Magyarország védőszentje.
items.english: The canonized king is today Hungary's patron saint.

items.spanish: Az utókorra megőrzött Intelmeket máig olvassák.
items.english: People still read the Admonitions, preserved for posterity.

items.spanish: A sokat tisztelt uralkodó emlékét minden év augusztus 20-án ünneplik.
items.english: The much-honored ruler's memory is celebrated every year on August 20th.

sections.content: By now you can build quite long titles simply by stacking participles before a noun: *a megkeresztelt, majd megkoronázott, végül szentté avatott István* — "the baptized, then crowned, and finally canonized István". Each participle stays unchanged; only their order tells the story.
